Machines above Moston and lights over Levenshulme: Every UFO reported over Greater Manchester mapped

A ‘large black triangle’ featuring a red light on each point was witnessed hovering over Stretford last year

17:08, 31 Oct 2026Updated 17:09, 31 Oct 2026

It is a question that has haunted humanity for centuries: Are we alone in the universe? If not, have any of the other civilisations that might exist elsewhere in the cosmos have ever come to Earth.

‌

‌

A more niche question might be: have any of them ever flown 50,000 light years to hover over Bolton for a bit?

‌

With Halloween falling on Saturday (October 31), the nation is getting into the spirit of dressing up as some of their favourite spooky characters and creatures. Many of them will be dressing up as aliens.

‌

It’s hard to pinpoint exactly where the obsession with UFOs began. For some it was seeing Steven Spielberg’s ET in the cinema, while others spent years binge watching The X Files just to catch a glimpse of the creatures beyond our knowledge.

Nearly 2,000 Unidentified Flying Objects (UFOs) have been documented and logged in the UK over the last five years by research group UFO Identified - including dozens over Greater Manchester.

‌

Now, a searchable interactive map allows you to explore every unexplained encounter logged in your area between 2021 and 2026.

Despite orbs, spheres and ‘star-like’ sightings making up the bulk of British sightings, researchers have logged 164 reports of similar wedge-shaped objects. This means that roughly one in every 12 sightings involves a distinctive triangle.

‌

For years on end, witnesses across the UK have reported seeing dark, matte triangles gliding soundlessly at low altitude over housing estates, farmland, and coastal areas before darting away at incredible speeds.

‌

Back in July, a ‘large black triangle’ featuring a red light on each point was witnessed hovering over Stretford in Greater Manchester for more than 30 minutes. Other sightings have been made over Levenshulme, Moston, Salford and elsewhere across the city-region.

‌

Ash Ellis, founder of UFO Identified, said: “There are thousands of people across the UK who have seen something they could not readily explain, but the reports are often difficult to find once the initial interest has passed.

“We wanted to build a serious, easy-to-use public archive that keeps those accounts accessible and allows people to look for patterns for themselves.”
